raw.query: SELECT l.policy, l.ttft_p99_ms AS live_ttft_p99_ms, lat.p99_ms AS offline_ttft_p99_ms, ROUND(((l.ttft_p99_ms - lat.p99_ms) / lat.p99_ms * 100)::numeric, 2) AS ttft_diff_pct, l.replica_seconds AS live_replica_s, c.provisioned_worker_seconds AS offline_replica_s, ROUND(((l.replica_seconds - c.provisioned_worker_seconds) / c.provisioned_worker_seconds * 100)::numeric, 2) AS replica_diff_pct FROM provenance.v_live_anchor l JOIN provenance.v_pool_latency lat ON lat.run_id = CASE WHEN l.policy = 'forecast' THEN 'a11:burst3_fc_chronos_L60' ELSE 'a11:burst3_reactive_L60' END AND lat.sla_metric = 'ttft' AND lat.is_current = true JOIN provenance.v_pool_cost c ON c.run_id = CASE WHEN l.policy = 'forecast' THEN 'a11:burst3_fc_chronos_L60' ELSE 'a11:burst3_reactive_L60' END AND c.is_current = true;
raw.observed: TTFT p99 differences are 1.05% (reactive) and 6.76% (forecast); replica-time differences are -5.26% (forecast) and -7.71% (reactive)
raw.claimed: TTFT p99 differences within 1.1-6.8%, provisioned replica-time within 8%
raw.evidence: Live validation anchor (v_live_anchor) vs offline twins (v_pool_latency & v_pool_cost) perfectly corroborates that TTFT p99 bounds land in [1.05%, 6.76%] and replica-seconds bounds in [5.26%, 7.71%] (both under 8%).
